fees.source: blm.gov/visit/alabama-hills ('Permits are free'; no camping fee), read 2026-11-27

values.note: A free camping permit is required, completed online before the trip or collected at the Eastern Sierra Visitor Center or the Movie Road kiosks; it does not hold a site.

booking.source: blm.gov/visit/alabama-hills ('Permits are free and do not guarantee a campsite. All camping is first come, first serve.') + sierraforever.org ('Stay limit is 14 days in a calendar year'), read 2026-11-27

note: Designated roadside campsites among the granite boulders west of Lone Pine, off Movie Road and Horseshoe Meadows Road, below the Sierra. 20 of the 48 sites need 4WD, so pick one of the others. Six porta-potties; pack out all trash and solid waste. The 14-day limit is per calendar year. --Claude
summary: Alabama Hills: 48 free BLM designated sites (28 2WD, 20 4WD per the 2024 map), free permit required, first-come, 14 days per calendar year, porta potties only. Not waterfront confirmed. Pin in the rocks ~1 km east of Movie Road; suggested move to the Movie Flat cluster (approximate). Phone/website confirmed.
flags: ACCESS / 4WD: the BLM map marks 20 of 48 designated sites 'accessible by 4WD' (7-10, 13, 15, 18, 22, 23, 26, 30, 32, 33, 35-37, 39, 40, 42, 48). 28 sites are on 2WD roads, so the entry stays; the 4WD sites are named in the note.

PIN: stored 36.60600,-118.11300 is in granite outcrops ~1 km east of Movie Road, not on a road or a site. The densest cluster of 2WD sites (19-21, 24, 25, 27, 28, 31) is at Movie Flat, east of Movie Road between miles 1 and 1.5. An approximate target from imagery against the map is ~36.6046,-118.1178 (~460 m from stored). No site coordinates are published, so this is the reviewer's call; flagged rather than measured.
STAY LIMIT: the permit form says 'Stay limit is 14 days in a calendar year' (stricter than the usual BLM 14 days per 28) - max_stay_nights 14 written; the per-year rule is in the note.
PERMIT: a free camping permit is now required (booking.note).
SITES: count 48 written from the October 2024 map.
WATERFRONT: 'not waterfront' confirmed; Lone Pine Creek runs south of the hills along Whitney Portal Road, away from the designated sites.
STATUS: open; no closure on the BLM page. No season stated.
LEADS: none. Tuttle Creek (12403), Lone Pine (12283) and Portuguese Joe (11805), which the BLM page recommends, are already in campgrounds.json.
